content.value_statement: Paid-ad tests can produce misleading results when variants, sample size, and decision rules are unclear. This skill creates a documented test plan or read-out with separate statistical and practical-effect checks.
actual_capabilities: Creates falsifiable hypotheses for creative and landing-page tests.
Builds A/B/n matrices that isolate one variable per variant.
Defines primary metrics, contextual metrics, and guardrails.
Plans sample size, duration, power, and read policies.
Interprets supplied conversion or continuous-metric results.
Separates statistical evidence from practical impact and approved decisions.
limitations: It uses only data supplied by the user or manually exported results.
It does not create ad variants or operate advertising platforms.
It does not choose a business action without a named owner and precommitted rule.
It cannot correct biased tracking, invalid randomization, or missing source data.

use_cases.title: Plan a landing-page test
use_cases.description: Define a controlled hero or CTA experiment with metrics, sample size, duration, and guardrails.

use_cases.title: Review a finished campaign experiment
use_cases.description: Calculate effect size, uncertainty, statistical status, and practical-effect status from a results export.

use_cases.title: Design an incrementality study
use_cases.description: Outline treatment and holdout groups, a measurement window, and an owner-governed decision rule.

prompt_templates.title: Start a simple A/B test
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an A/B test for two landing-page hero variants. Our baseline conversion rate is 3%, and we want to detect a 15% lift.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a creative matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an A/B/n test plan for four search ad creatives. Include one isolated change per variant, primary metrics, guardrails, sample size, and duration.

prompt_templates.title: Read a results export
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my test results with control and variant sessions and conversions. Report the effect, uncertainty, statistical status, practical-effect status, and missing decision inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an incrementality study
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a geo-holdout incrementality test for this campaign. State matching requirements, success metrics, sample window, guardrails, and a precommitted owner decision rule.

output_examples.input: Baseline conversion rate is 3%, traffic is 5,000 sessions daily, and the minimum meaningful lift is 15%.
output: Falsifiable hypothesis with one proposed change.
Per-variant sample target and estimated run duration.
Primary conversion metric, guardrails, and declared alpha and power.

output_examples.input: Control: 10,000 sessions and 300 conversions. Variant: 10,100 sessions and 330 conversions.
output: Conversion rates and relative lift with a confidence interval.
Decision marked undecided unless an owner and rule were precommitted.

best_practices: Precommit the hypothesis, minimum detectable effect, alpha, power, and stopping policy before launch.
Change only one variable per variant and retain a control group.
Define decision ownership and guardrail rules before viewing results.
anti_patterns: Do not stop a test early because a temporary result looks favorable.
Do not treat a p-value as an automatic promote or rollback decision.
Do not combine several creative or landing-page changes in one variant.

faq.question: Can this skill create ad copy or landing-page variants?
faq.answer: No. It designs and evaluates tests. Use a creative-building workflow to produce variants.

faq.question: What data is needed for a test design?
faq.answer: Provide a baseline rate, expected traffic, and the minimum lift worth detecting.

faq.question: What data is needed for a result read-out?
faq.answer: Provide per-variant exposures and conversions, or the relevant continuous metric samples.

faq.question: Does it access advertising accounts?
faq.answer: No. It works with user-provided or manually exported data.

faq.question: Will it tell me to promote a winner?
faq.answer: Only when a named owner and precommitted action rule are provided. Otherwise it returns an undecided decision.

faq.question: Does statistical significance prove business value?
faq.answer: No. The skill reports statistical and practical-effect checks separately.
